maria: Heads-up: I found a reproducible bug where AsyncClient streaming + retry leads to a suppressed CancelledError and user code never sees the final exception. repro and notes below. anyone run into this?

maria: minimal repro (local flaky backend to trigger 5xx):
```py
import asyncio

async def consume(gen):
    async for chunk in gen:
        print('got', chunk)

async def main():
    gen = client.generate_stream('hello', idempotency_key='k-1')
    t = asyncio.create_task(consume(gen))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.15)  # let stream start and maybe hit 5xx/replay
    await client.close()  # simulate app shutdown while replay in-flight
    await t
```

maria: observed log line: `Task exception was never retrieved` pointing at AsyncClient._stream_to_queue -> CancelledError. user sees partial output from the `async for` and no exception raised.

alex: which sdk version? can you paste the full traceback?

maria: v0.12.3. log snippet:
```
Task exception was never retrieved
future: <Task finished name='Task-17' coro=<AsyncClient._stream_to_queue() done, defined at /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood_sdk/async_client.py:402> exception=CancelledError()>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/.../site-packages/redwood_sdk/async_client.py", line 410, in _stream_to_queue
    chunk = await resp.content.readchunk()
asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError
```

maria: The background task is cancelled during replay/close and the exception isn't bubbled out of the async generator.

ben: This matches a prior bug: we spawn a background task to push stream chunks into a queue and we cancel tasks in close() but don't await them, leaving unhandled exceptions. Two issues: (1) noisy suppressed exceptions in logs, (2) generator semantics — the consumer should get an exception for fatal errors.

riya: And the retry/replay logic complicates it: on transient 5xx we attempt a replay using the idempotency token and feed cached prefix chunks; if we cancel mid-replay we can leave a producer orphaned.

maria: Exactly. repro triggered a 502 after some cached chunks were emitted; client tried to replay, then I called close(). result: partial output, no exception.

alex: Proposed immediate mitigation: ensure produced tasks are awaited on generator close or attach done-callbacks that re-raise/log exceptions so they don't become "Task exception was never retrieved". Longer-term: change generator plumbing to await producer completion and re-raise its exception from the generator.

ben: Implementation plan: 1) hotfix -> add `task.add_done_callback(_ensure_log_and_raise)` and track tasks to await them in close() (non-breaking). 2) follow-up -> revamp generate_stream to use `asyncio.TaskGroup` (Python 3.11+) or an explicit awaitable producer/consumer pattern guaranteeing exceptions propagate to the async iterator consumer. add tests.

riya: Typing/SDK notes: generate_stream is annotated as `AsyncIterator[str]`. If we change behavior to raise on underlying transport/retry errors that's consistent with iterator semantics, but we should document raised exceptions (ClientConnectionError, RetryError) in docstrings and update stubs/py.typed. onboarding docs should call out that streams can raise on transient failures.

sam: This impacts sample apps: users see truncated model outputs and assume hallucination. P0 DX hit. we should ship the hotfix as a patch release on 0.12.x if tests pass.

alex: One design choice: (A) make streams raise on first unrecoverable error (semantic change, preferred), or (B) keep returning partial output and emit a terminal `error` chunk (backwards compatible for some consumers). I favor (A) — aligns with Python iterator error semantics.

ben: I'll draft a PR implementing the hotfix + tests that assert (i) `async for` raises RetryError on server 5xx during replay, and (ii) no "Task exception was never retrieved" emitted in logs. also include an integration test for idempotency token: ensure replay uses same token and doesn't double-execute non-idempotent endpoints.

riya: Can we also emit telemetry: `replay.attempt`, `replay.success`, `replay.failure` events with idempotency token and model/version metadata? ops asked for visibility into replays causing partial outputs.

deploy-bot: CI: redwood/py-sdk #3724 failed on master 1:34 UTC — https://ci.internal/redwood/py-sdk/3724

ben: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/4557 — includes hotfix + unit/integration tests. requesting reviews from @alex @riya.

maria: Verified locally with PR patch applied: my repro now raises `RetryError` inside the `async for` and logs are clean. thanks.

alex: Follow-ups: update CHANGELOG with migration notes, add optional param `raise_on_partial=True` to generate_stream for backwards-compatible control, and update SDK docs + examples in `examples/streaming/README.md`.

sam: If PR approved, i'll backport to 0.12.x and cut a patch release. pls include changelog blurb and a short migration snippet for app authors.

ben: Will add docstring `Raises:` and update type stubs. Also add a test that ensures streaming consumers are able to catch `RetryError` and handle cleanup properly.

maria: Thanks all — I'll open a separate small issue about adding a lint rule to detect background tasks without awaiting/keeping references. helps prevent similar bugs.

sam: Great. marking this one P0 for DX until patch is released.

maria: I'll attach my failing test file to the PR: `tests/streaming/test_replay_cancel.py`.

ben: Noted. merging after approvals. :thumbsup:

maria: resolved for me with the patch. will follow up if anything else shows up.
